body:
## Why

The tracked-variable schema for this repo does not need to be invented. Two comparison tools already run in the work environment with real, named field sets, and the response gives them verbatim (section D). Adopting those names is what makes a tool built here interoperable with the tools already in use there; inventing parallel names is the single change most likely to make this repo useless.

Evidence: response section D, the consultant-report comparison tool and the legal-document lineage tool (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md).

## Scope

A schema module plus JSON Schema files for the record types those two tools already emit, expressed once so both a consultant-report comparison and a legal-document comparison populate the same shapes.

## Non-Goals

- No renaming for elegance. Where the existing tools have a field name, that name wins even if a better one exists.
- No comparison logic in this issue. Schema and validation only.
- No new materiality judgments. The tier vocabularies are adopted as data, not re-derived.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/schema/change_ledger.py` with fields `doc_type, transition, canonical_section, subsection, item, page_new, change_type, tier, topic, prior_text, current_text`.
- [ ] Add `continuity_ledger` with `doc_type, transition, canonical_section, status, words_current, carry_forward_pct, refresh_pct, verbatim_words, near_verbatim_words, revised_words, new_words, dropped_words, segments_verbatim, segments_near, segments_revised, segments_new, segments_dropped, segments_cosmetic, new_items, dropped_items`.
- [ ] Add `persistence_ledger` with `doc_type, canonical_section, item, consecutive_years_unchanged, first_seen, last_seen, words, text`, and `stale_flag_ledger` as that shape plus `report_year, flag`.
- [ ] Add `section_crosswalk` with `doc_type, year, raw_section, canonical_section, words`.
- [ ] Add `material_ledger` with the legal tool's seven columns `date, tier, theme, category, change, from_value, to_value`, documenting that `from` and `to` are reserved words in Python and that the wire names stay `From` and `To`.
- [ ] Define the segment classification vocabulary as a closed enumeration `VERBATIM, NEAR_VERBATIM, REVISED, NEW, DROPPED`, and the materiality tiers as `T1` decision-relevant, `T2` factual refresh, `T3` cosmetic.
- [ ] Publish JSON Schema for each record type under `schemas/` and validate every fixture against it in tests.
- [ ] Add a round-trip test that a ledger row serializes to the wire names the existing tools use and parses back unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every field name listed above exists with that exact wire spelling, asserted by a test that reads the names from the JSON Schema rather than from Python identifiers.
- [ ] The segment vocabulary and tier set reject an unknown value rather than passing it through.
- [ ] A row with a non-finite number in any percentage or word-count field is rejected at validation, not stored.
- [ ] Fixtures exist for both a consultant-report transition and a legal-filing transition, and both validate.

## Test Gate

`tests/test_schema_wire_names.py`, run by this repo's CI gate. Demonstrate it by deliberately renaming `carry_forward_pct` to `carryforward_pct` in the schema, confirming the wire-name test fails, then reverting and confirming it passes. Record both in the pull request.

## Implementation Notes

The percentage fields carry a trap worth encoding: figures computed against recognized rather than native text are a floor, not a precise value (response section D). Add an explicit `text_basis` field of `native | ocr | mixed` to the continuity ledger so a downstream reader can tell which figures are floors.
title: Adopt the two existing work tools' ledger schemas verbatim
